questions.stem_text:
Dworkin contends that to every legal question there is only one right answer. Which
proposition below is most inconsistent with this claim?

options.A: In hard cases judges generally decide cases on the basis of rights.
options.B: The rights of the parties feature in the determination of most cases before the courts.
options.D: Judges seek the best 'fit' with constitutional and institutional history.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - Judges exercise strong discretion.

questions.stem_text: Which one of the following doctrines is not associated with Natural Law thinking
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Doctrine of substituted security

questions.stem_text: Which statement below best represents Durkheim's view of the function of punishment?

Which statement below is the least likely to follow logically from Savigny's notion of a
Volksgeist?

options.A: A society's law is a reflection of its culture.
options.C: Law is the deliberate expression of a sovereign's will.
options.D: Law is an integral element of the social fabric.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - Law is the deliberate expression of a sovereign's will.

questions.stem_text:
Robert Nozick's proposes the formula r x H as a guide to determine the appropriate
punishment. What does it mean?

options.A: Effectiveness of rehabilitation of multiplied by hazard to the community.
options.B: Extent of responsibility multiplied by actual harm done.
options.C: Risk of violence multiplied by degree of humility of offender.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - Extent of responsibility multiplied by actual harm done.

Discuss the rationale behind the exhaustion of local remedies in international human
rights law, highlighting its implications for local courts and international tribunals.
questions.gold_answer:
The local remedies rule aims on the one hand to restrict the volume of petitions to
international tribunals while at the same time building up the capacity of local courts.
